_comment: THE admin-cli <-> actor-control WORKER SEAM. Machine-checked from BOTH sides.
D-PC-SEAM-NO-CONTRACT. This seam spans two services and two languages joined by
nothing but a process boundary: Go renders argv in `workerArgs`, Rust parses it in
`Args::parse`; Rust emits one JSON object in `emit`, Go unmarshals it into
`ActorControlOutcome`. Two lists in two languages with no compiler between them —
a rename on either side keeps BOTH unit suites green and breaks the live loop.
That is the shape the Frontend-Tool Contract standard exists for, and this file is
that standard's own pattern applied one seam over.
It was NOT unguarded before this file: `RunActorControl` refuses an outcome the
worker did not name and a created actor with no id, and the invoker cross-checks
the echoed ids. Those are runtime guards on the load-bearing fields, discovered by
an operator at the moment of failure. This is a test.
AUTHORED FROM MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-20 — every entry below was read out of the two
sources, not recalled. Both sides agreed at the time of writing (18 JSON keys, 8
flags, 3 ops), so this file freezes an agreement rather than declaring one.
TO CHANGE THE SEAM: edit this file in the SAME COMMIT as both sides. The two tests
read it at runtime, so a contract-only edit reds them without recompiling either.
Rust: services/world-service/tests/worker_seam_contract.rs
Go:   services/admin-cli/internal/commands/actor_control_seam_test.go
Every flag Go may render and Rust must accept. `--dry-run` is value-less; the
rest take one argument. A flag Go renders that Rust does not parse is an
`unknown flag` exit 2 two processes from where it was typed — which is exactly
how far apart the two lists are without this file.
Every key that may appear on the worker's stdout, and which Go reads. Asserted as
a SET in both directions: a key Rust emits that Go does not read is silently
dropped, and a key Go reads that Rust never emits is a field that is always the
zero value — the write-only-behaviour bug, one process over.
Closed sets. `status` and `outcome` are what an operator's script matches on, so
a rename is a breaking change to something nobody compiles.
`actor_created` appears here and NOT in `actor_control_flow::Outcome`: the flow
enum covers the four grant/revoke results, and create-actor's outcome word is
written by the worker directly. Recorded because the asymmetry is real and a
reader looking for a fifth enum variant will not find one.
The verdict. Parsed by `SubprocessActorControlInvoker.Run`, which treats 2 as
'nothing was attempted' and reads `conflict` out of the JSON on 1 to decide
whether the operator should reload and decide or go look at the bridge.
exit_codes.0: the operation succeeded, or the dry run completed
exit_codes.1: refused or failed; stdout carries `error`, and `conflict` says which
